subject.title: [Bug]: tools/sandbox: MEDIA_MAX_BYTES (5 MB) is hardcoded and not user-configurable

question: Should OpenClaw expose a configurable global media-store/sandbox staging cap, or should it keep the 5 MiB default and only fix narrow channel/document paths such as Telegram reply-media?
rationale: The issue is source-reproducible, but changing the generic cap affects disk/resource limits and sandbox media exposure, and AGENTS.md treats new config/default surfaces as product and security-sensitive.

options.title: Approve bounded config
options.body: Add a documented bounded config surface for the generic media store and sandbox staging cap, plus tests and security-oriented limits.

options.title: Narrow channel fixes only
options.body: Keep the generic 5 MiB cap and land targeted channel/document fixes where downstream limits already allow larger payloads.

options.title: Close as intentional limit
options.body: Treat the 5 MiB generic staging cap as a deliberate safety default and ask users to use channel/account caps or smaller files.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded config
recommendation.body: Add a documented bounded config surface for the generic media store and sandbox staging cap, plus tests and security-oriented limits.

likelyOwner.reason: The broad cap and sandbox staging provenance traces most directly to Peter Steinberger's media-store and sandbox-staging history.
